public_rationale: Anthropic stated on June 12 that it was removing access to both models for all users to comply with the government directive. Congressional correspondence identifies the underlying action as Commerce's June 12 export restriction. Later restoration is consistent with Marcus's qualification that the shutdown might be temporary.
limitations: The evidence establishes suspended customer access, not cessation of all internal model activity.
The causal account relies principally on Anthropic's contemporaneous disclosure.
The speculative industry-crisis language is not assessed.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The Commerce Department's June 2026 export control order has basically led to the possibly temporary shutdown of Anthropic's Fable and Mythos.

statement.excerpt: Now let’s consider last night’s Commerce Department cut-off-your-nose-to-spite-your-face export control order, which has basically led to the (temporary?) shutdown of Fable and Mythos, perhaps sparking a crisis in the US AI industry.
statement.document_title: The White House’s shambolic AI policy

our_interpretation: 'Shutdown' means suspension of customer access to both models, not deletion of model weights or cessation of all internal work.
'Led to' includes a suspension implemented by Anthropic to comply with the directive.
The event window is June 12–13, 2026, as established by 'last night' in the June 13 post.
The tentative suggestion of an industry crisis is outside the normalized causal claim.
criteria.support_condition: Dated records establish that customer access to both models was suspended in response to the Commerce directive within the event window.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable records establish that access was not materially suspended, only one model was affected, or the suspension had an independent cause rather than the directive.
